'''Ellen D. Ketterson''' is an American evolutionary biologist, [[Behavioral ecology|behavioral ecologist]], [[Neuroendocrinology|neuroendocrinologist]] and [[Ornithology|ornithologist]] best known for her experimental approach to the study of life-history trade-offs in a songbird, the [[dark-eyed junco|Dark-eyed Junco]]. She is currently a Distinguished Professor of Biology, Director of the [[Environmental Resilience Institute]], and affiliate professor in Cognitive Science, Gender Studies, Integrative Study of Animal Behavior, and Neuroscience at [[Indiana University]].

==Education and career==
Ketterson obtained all of her degrees from [[Indiana University Bloomington]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150606124321/http://www.indiana.edu/~kettlab/people/ellen/Departmental%20CV%20Ketterson%20Jan%202015.pdf |title=Departmental CV — Ellen D. Ketterson |date=January 2015 |website=www.indiana.edu |archive-date=2015-06-06 |url-status=dead |url=http://www.indiana.edu/~kettlab/people/ellen/Departmental%20CV%20Ketterson%20Jan%202015.pdf |access-date=2018-10-16}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |url=http://newsinfo.iu.edu/news-archive/3166.html |title=Ellen D. Ketterson: IU News Room: Indiana University |website=newsinfo.iu.edu |access-date=2018-10-17}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://indianapublicmedia.org/profiles/evolutionary-biologist-ellen-ketterson/ |title=Evolutionary Biologist Ellen Ketterson |work=Profiles — Indiana Public Media |access-date=2018-10-17}}</ref> She earned an A.B. in 1966 and an M.A. in 1968, both in [[Botany]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> She received her Ph.D. in 1974 in [[Zoology]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

After receiving her doctoral degree, Ketterson was a postdoctoral scholar from 1974 to 1975 at [[Washington State University]] working with avian environmental physiologist [[James R. King]].<ref name=":0" /> She was an assistant professor at [[Bowling Green State University]] from 1975 to 1977 before joining the faculty in the Department of Biology at [[Indiana University]] in 1977.<ref name=":0" /> Ketterson was appointed as a Distinguished Professor of Biology at Indiana University in 2006. <ref name=":0" /> She was also appointed as an affiliated faculty member of the Gender Studies department in 2003 and as a program faculty member of the Cognitive Science department in 2006 at Indiana University.<ref name=":0" /> 

Ketterson co-founded the [https://animalbehavior.indiana.edu/ Center for the Integrative Study of Animal Behavior] at Indiana University and served as the co-director from 1990 to 2002.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> Ketterson has been a senior research fellow at the [[Kinsey Institute|Kinsey Institute for Research on Sex, Gender, and Reproduction]] at Indiana University since 2007.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> Since 2017, Ketterson has served as the director of the [https://eri.iu.edu/index.html Environmental Resilience Institute] at Indiana University, which aims to predict impacts of environmental change and develop solutions to prepare [[Indiana]] businesses, farmers, communities and individuals for those impacts.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://eri.iu.edu/about-us/leadership/index.html|title=Leadership|website=Environmental Resilience Institute Part of the Prepared for Environmental Change Grand Challenge|language=en-US|access-date=2018-10-17|archive-date=2018-10-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181017123532/https://eri.iu.edu/about-us/leadership/index.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://news.iu.edu/stories/2018/09/iu/releases/13-environmental-resilience-institute-toolkit-environmental-change.html|title=IU launches toolkit to help communities cope with environmental change|work=News at IU|access-date=2018-10-17|language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2004, Ketterson received a [[Guggenheim Fellowship|Guggenheim fellowship]] to study plumage variation in [[junco]] species across North and Central America.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> Ketterson served as the president of the [[American Society of Naturalists]] in 2015.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amnat.org/about/history/past-ec.html|title=Past Officers of the ASN|website=www.amnat.org|language=en|access-date=2018-10-17}}</ref> She has also won several major awards recognizing her career achievements in ornithology, including the [[American Ornithological Society]] Elliott Couse Award (1996), [[Wilson Ornithological Society]] [[Margaret Morse Nice Medal]] (awarded jointly with [[Val Nolan, Jr.]] in 1998), and the Alden Miller Award from the [[Cooper Ornithological Society]] (2014).<ref name=":0" /> She is also a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] and the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science|American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)]].<ref name=":0" />

==Research==
Ketterson and her trainees, with her longtime collaborator and partner [[Val Nolan, Jr.]], have conducted long-term field studies combined with experimental manipulation of free-living [[dark-eyed junco]]s at the [[Mountain Lake (Virginia)|Mountain Lake Biological Station]] in Virginia since the 1970s.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.amnat.org/membership/members/EllenKetterson.html |title=Ellen Ketterson |website=www.amnat.org |language=en |access-date=2018-10-17}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |url=https://mlbs.virginia.edu/ |title=Mountain Lake Biological Station, U.Va. |website=mlbs.virginia.edu|language=en |access-date=2018-10-17}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |url=https://ketterson.lab.indiana.edu/research/virginia.html |title=Virginia: Research: Ketterson Lab: Indiana University Bloomington |website=Ketterson Lab|language=en-US |access-date=2018-10-17 |archive-date=2018-10-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181017123537/https://ketterson.lab.indiana.edu/research/virginia.html |url-status=dead}}</ref> Early in her career, Ketterson focused on differential migration {{em dash}} specifically on a pattern of movement in which female birds migrate farther than males.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ketterson |first1=Ellen D. |last2=Nolan |first2=Val |date=July 1976 |title=Geographic Variation and Its Climatic Correlates in the Sex Ratio of Eastern-Wintering Dark-Eyed Juncos (Junco Hyemalis Hyemalis) |journal=Ecology |language=en |volume=57 |issue=4 |pages=679–693 |doi=10.2307/1936182 |issn=0012-9658 |jstor=1936182 |bibcode=1976Ecol...57..679K }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Ketterson |first1=Ellen D. |title=The Evolution of Differential Bird Migration |date=1983 |series =Current Ornithology |pages=357–402 |publisher=Springer US |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-1-4615-6781-3_12 |isbn=9781461567837 |last2=Nolan |first2=Val}}</ref>

Ketterson developed the experimental approach of manipulating levels of the hormone [[testosterone]] in free-living birds and comparing behavior, physiology, and fitness to controls in order to study the evolution of [[Life history theory|life-history]] trade-offs.<ref name=":5">{{Cite journal |last1=Ketterson |first1=Ellen D. |last2=Nolan |first2=Val |date=Nov 1992 |title=Hormones and Life Histories: An Integrative Approach |journal=The American Naturalist |language=en |volume=140 |pages=S33–S62 |doi=10.1086/285396 |pmid=19426026 |bibcode=1992ANat..140S..33K |issn=0003-0147 |hdl=2022/17322 |s2cid=44692155 |hdl-access=free}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite journal |last1=Ketterson |first1=Ellen D. |last2=Nolan |first2=Val |last3=Wolf |first3=Licia |last4=Ziegenfus |first4=Charles |date=Dec 1992 |title=Testosterone and Avian Life Histories: Effects of Experimentally Elevated Testosterone on Behavior and Correlates of Fitness in the Dark-Eyed Junco (Junco hyemalis) |journal=The American Naturalist |language=en |volume=140 |issue=6 |pages=980–999 |doi=10.1086/285451 |bibcode=1992ANat..140..980K |issn=0003-0147 |hdl=2022/17323 |s2cid=56413684 |url=https://scholarworks.iu.edu/dspace/bitstream/2022/17323/1/TestosteroneAndAvianLifeHistories.pdf |hdl-access=free}}</ref><ref name=":6">{{Cite journal |last1=Ketterson |first1=Ellen D. |last2=Nolan |first2=Val |last3=Cawthorn |first3=Michelle J. |last4=Parker |first4=Patricia G. |last5=Ziegenfus |first5=Charles |date=2008-06-28 |title=Phenotypic engineering: using hormones to explore the mechanistic and functional bases of phenotypic variation in nature |journal=Ibis |language=en |volume=138 |issue=1 |pages=70–86 |doi=10.1111/j.1474-919x.1996.tb04314.x |issn=0019-1019}}</ref> She coined the term "phenotypic engineering" to describe this approach.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6" /> Ketterson's research showed that experimentally-elevated levels of [[testosterone]] increased male aggression, reduced parental care, and increased singing in males.<ref name=":4" /> In addition, males given exogenous testosterone were preferred by females in [[mate choice | mate-choice]] tests.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1997-11-01 |title=Testosterone and mate choice in the dark-eyed junco |journal=Animal Behaviour |language=en |volume=54 |issue=5 |pages=1135–1146 |doi=10.1006/anbe.1997.0555 |issn=0003-3472 |last1=Enstrom |first1=David A. |last2=Ketterson |first2=Ellen D. |last3=Nolan, Jr |first3=VAL |bibcode=1997AnBeh..54.1135E |s2cid=6826752 }}</ref> They also exhibited higher reproductive success as a result of extra-pair fertilizations despite the lower success of broods that they parent.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Raouf |first1=Samrrah A. |last2=Parker |first2=Patricia G. |last3=Ketterson |first3=Ellen D. |last4=Nolan |first4=Val |last5=Ziegenfus |first5=Charles |date=1997-11-22 |title=Testosterone affects reproductive success by influencing extra–pair fertilizations in male dark–eyed juncos (Aves: Junco hyemalis) |journal=Proceedings of the Royal Society of London B: Biological Sciences |language=en |volume=264 |issue=1388 |pages=1599–1603 |doi=10.1098/rspb.1997.0223 |pmc=1688731 |issn=0962-8452}}</ref> However, she also found that testosterone-treated males had shorter life-spans<ref name=":4" /> and reduced [[immune-system]] function.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Casto |first1=Joseph M. |last2=Nolan, Jr. |first2=Val |last3=Ketterson |first3=Ellen D. |date=Apr 2001 |title=Steroid Hormones and Immune Function: Experimental Studies in Wild and Captive Dark-Eyed Juncos (Junco hyemalis) |journal=The American Naturalist |language=en |volume=157 |issue=4 |pages=408–420 |doi=10.1086/319318 |pmid=18707250 |bibcode=2001ANat..157..408C |s2cid=16296790 |issn=0003-0147}}</ref> Her research has provided a mechanistic understanding of the fitness consequences of how animals allocate time and energy to competing demands (i.e. reproduction versus survival).

Later, her work explored whether [[hormone]]s, which affect multiple target-tissues simultaneously and mediate coordinated suites of traits, either constrain or potentiate adaptation.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ketterson |first1=Ellen D.|last2=Nolan, Jr.|first2=Val |date=July 1999 |title=Adaptation, Exaptation, and Constraint: A Hormonal Perspective |journal=The American Naturalist |language=en |volume=154 |issue=S1 |pages=S4–S25 |doi=10.1086/303280 |pmid=29586711|bibcode=1999ANat..154S...4K |issn=0003-0147 |hdl=2022/17324 |s2cid=4376696 |hdl-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=McGlothlin |first1=Joel W. |last2=Ketterson |first2=Ellen D. |date=2008-05-12 |title=Hormone-mediated suites as adaptations and evolutionary constraints |journal=Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London B: Biological Sciences |language=en |volume=363 |issue=1497 |pages=1611–1620 |doi=10.1098/rstb.2007.0002 |issn=0962-8436 |pmid=18048296 |pmc=2606720}}</ref> This work foreshadowed her interest in addressing limits to organisms' ability to respond to environmental change and the role of hormonally-mediated seasonal timing  of behaviors (like reproduction, [[Moulting|molt]], and migration) in the generation and loss of [[biodiversity]]. As the director of the [https://eri.iu.edu/index.html Environmental Resilience Institute], she leads a team of [[Indiana University]] researchers to prepare the [[Hoosier]] state for the effects of on-going [[environmental change]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://news.iu.edu/stories/2017/05/iu/releases/10-grand-challenges.html |title=New IU Grand Challenge initiative to tackle environmental threats |last=Fryling |first=Kevin |work=News at IU |access-date=2018-10-17 |language=en-US | quote = [...]  IU researchers – led by internationally acclaimed scientist Ellen Ketterson, IU Distinguished Professor of Biology – will build Indiana-specific projections of environmental change that equip governments, businesses and community groups to respond with the right investments in agriculture, industry, infrastructure, and public health and safety. }}</ref>

The Ketterson research group currently conducts field research at a number of sites throughout the range of [[junco]] species, including in Indiana at Kent Farm on the Indiana University Research and Teaching Preserve,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://preserve.indiana.edu/about/kent-farm.html |title=Kent Farm: About Us: Research and Teaching Preserve : Indiana University |website=Research and Teaching Preserve |language=en-US |access-date=2018-10-17}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://ketterson.lab.indiana.edu/research/indiana.html |title=Indiana: Research: Ketterson Lab: Indiana University Bloomington |website=Ketterson Lab |language=en-US |access-date=2018-10-17 |archive-date=2018-10-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181017123617/https://ketterson.lab.indiana.edu/research/indiana.html |url-status=dead}}</ref> in the Appalachian Mountains in Virginia at the [[Mountain Lake (Virginia)|Mountain Lakes Biological Station]],<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /> in California on the [[University of California, San Diego]] campus and at [[Laguna Mountain Recreation Area |Laguna |language=en-US |access-date=2018-10-17 |archive-date=2018-10-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181017123548/https://ketterson.lab.indiana.edu/research/california.html |url-status=dead}}</ref> in northwest Wyoming at [[Grand Teton National Park]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://ketterson.lab.indiana.edu/research/wyoming.html |title=Wyoming: Research: Ketterson Lab: |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181017082224/https://ketterson.lab.indiana.edu/research/wyoming.html |url-status=dead}}</ref> in Idaho,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://ketterson.lab.indiana.edu/research/idaho.html |title=Idaho: Research: Ketterson Lab: Indiana University Bloomington |website=Ketterson Lab |language=en-US |access-date=2018-10-17 |archive-date=2018-10-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181017123616/https://ketterson.lab.indiana.edu/research/idaho.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> in South Dakota,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://ketterson.lab.indiana.edu/research/south%20dakota.html |title=South Dakota: Research: Ketterson Lab: Indiana University Bloomington |website=Ketterson Lab |language=en-US |access-date=2018-10-17 |archive-date=2018-10-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181017123528/https://ketterson.lab.indiana.edu/research/south%20dakota.html |url-status=dead}}</ref> in The 2013 documentary-film project, '[https://juncoproject.org/ Ordinary Extraordinary Junco: Remarkable Biology from a Backyard Bird]' highlights years of research conducted by Ketterson and her colleagues.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://newsinfo.iu.edu/news/page/normal/23556.html |title=With songbird as star, 'Ordinary Extraordinary Junco' movie puts spotlight on evolution, IU research: IU News Room: Indiana University |website=newsinfo.iu.edu |access-date=2018-10-17}}
</ref>

==Personal life==
Ketterson was married for 28 years to the ornithologist [[Val Nolan, Jr.]], her Ph.D. mentor and long-time collaborator, until his death in 2008.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Yakusawa|first=Ken|date=2008|title=In Memoriam: Val Nolan, Jr., 1920–2008|url=https://ketterson.lab.indiana.edu/doc/Nolan_obituary_Auk.pdf|journal=The Auk|volume=125|issue=3|pages=749–750|doi=10.1525/auk.2008.3708|s2cid=84653455|archive-date=2018-10-17|access-date=2018-10-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181017123613/https://ketterson.lab.indiana.edu/doc/Nolan_obituary_Auk.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

*Animal Behavior Society, Distinguished Animal Behaviorist Award, 2018<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://biology.indiana.edu/news-events/news/2018/ketterson-abs-award.html|title=Ketterson to receive Distinguished Animal Behaviorist Award|work=Department of Biology|access-date=2018-10-17|language=en-US}}</ref>
